post.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — The Civic Order
post.entry:
PRIVATE / GM-RESTRICTED

Vauntin Did Not Save Fogport Alone

Vauntin Quell did not cause the Catastrophe, but he was present when the royal Continuance Engine failed beneath House Heliot’s palace. He understood enough of the Engine’s purpose to recognize that the royal family’s emergency plan was failing. He chose to seal the palace and redirect the Engine’s preservation process rather than evacuate everyone inside.

That decision saved enough of Fogport to make his dictatorship possible. It also condemned thousands to become part of the city’s scars.

The Emergency Was Deliberately Kept Alive

Quell’s original emergency authority expired after the first year. He renewed it by manufacturing a series of manageable crises: food scares, sabotage panics, royalist plots, monster outbreaks, and carefully timed Civic Vigilance discoveries.

Most were real. Some were arranged. The Civic Order’s genius was learning that a real crisis could be made politically useful without being entirely invented.

The Royal Family

At least one member of the royal family survived the palace collapse. Quell knows this. The Office of Royal Remnants has spent forty-three years searching for them, but it is also being quietly manipulated by someone inside the Civic Order.

The surviving royal may not want the throne. They may want proof of what happened beneath the palace—and the names of everyone who chose to seal it.

The Civic Seven

The six living senators are not the only members of the Civic Seven. The seventh seat is occupied by a hidden voting mechanism beneath the old opera stage. It was built for the royal government and can still issue a legally valid civic vote.

Quell knows about it. He has never destroyed it because doing so would prove that the Civic Order’s legal continuity is false.

The Drip Cages

The submerged prison is not merely a punishment device. Its reservoir is connected to the old palace plumbing and reaches into tunnels beneath the Grand Promenade.

Some prisoners lowered into the water have heard machinery moving below them. A few have returned claiming that something beneath the Hall asked them to state their name, their future, and what they remembered of the Catastrophe.

The Bureaus Are Not Entirely Human

Several of the oldest departments continue following royal administrative procedures that no living official remembers creating. The Bureau of Plumbing Mysteries, the Office of Dream Recovery and Investment, and the Bureau of Shadow Analysis occasionally receive instructions stamped with the old royal seal.

The instructions are not always wrong.

Vauntin’s Real Fear

Vauntin is not primarily afraid of rebellion. He is afraid that Fogport will discover the truth and decide that his rule was unnecessary.

He can survive an assassin, a riot, or a royal claimant. He cannot survive the city realizing that it was saved by a machine, not by him.

GM Guidance

Do not reveal all of this at once. Let players discover the truth through concrete evidence: sealed records, surviving witnesses, contradictory bureau orders, old royal machinery, and people who were officially declared dead but continue to remember the palace.

These secrets should eventually resolve through play. The Civic Order is strange because it is hiding practical crimes beneath absurd administration—not because the truth is unknowable.
